description: Conformance corpus for async bindings and the async entry point. An `"async": true` binding hands the script a real promise; `executeAsync` (`execute_async` in Rust) runs its source as the body of an async function. Values in this file use the marker spelling of `spec/value-fidelity-tests.json`.
notes: The host binding `slow(ms, value)` returns a promise that resolves to `value` after `ms` milliseconds; `fail(message)` returns a promise that rejects with an `Error` carrying `message`. `sync()` is an ordinary binding that returns `"sync"`.

`body`: the runtime runs `script` through `executeAsync`, and the result must equal `expected`. The source is an async function body: `return` gives the result, `await` works at the top level, and a body that returns nothing yields `undefined`.

`promise`: the runtime runs `script` through `executeAsync`, and the result must equal `expected`. A case marked `concurrent` needs a runtime whose async bindings settle while the script keeps running; a runtime that settles an async binding before handing it to the script (Rust's `RuntimeMode::Sync`, C#) skips it.

`syncReach`: the runtime runs `script` through its synchronous `execute`; the script catches what calling the async binding threw and returns its message, which must begin with `error`. The runtime then runs `after` through `executeAsync`, whose result must equal `expected`: a refused call leaves the runtime usable. This applies to a runtime whose synchronous `execute` cannot drive an async binding (the universal JavaScript runtime, with either QuickJS build); a runtime that can (Node, Rust, C#) skips it.

`executeResult`: the runtime runs `script` through its synchronous `execute`, whose result is a promise. The JavaScript runtimes that cannot hand the host a settled value refuse it: `execute` throws an error whose message names `executeAsync`. A runtime that settles a promise result instead (Rust awaits it, C# drains its job queue before returning; see `spec/execution.md`) or hands the host the promise itself (Node) skips it.
`mod` is loaded into the runtime before the export sections run: its entry script registers the exports the cases invoke.

`exportAsync`: the runtime invokes `export` of the mod with `args` through its async export invocation (`invokeModExportAsync`, `invoke_export_async`, or the runtime's equivalent), which awaits a promise the export returns; the result must equal `expected`. An export reaches async bindings exactly as a script does: they hand it real promises. A case marked `concurrent` is skipped as in `promise`.

`exportSync`: the runtime invokes `export` with `args` through its synchronous export invocation, which must fail with an error whose message contains `error`: an export that ends in a promise is refused in favor of the async invocation, and an async binding it reaches is refused as from `execute`. The runtime then runs `after` through `executeAsync`, whose result must equal `expected`. This applies where `executeResult` and `syncReach` do; other runtimes skip it.

seesPromise.description: Reports whether an async binding hands it a promise.

startBinding.description: Returns slow(1, value) without awaiting it.

slow.description: Resolves to value after ms milliseconds.

fail.description: Rejects with an Error carrying message.

body.name: await works at the top level
body.script: var a = await 'x'; await null; return a + 'y';

body.name: a body that returns nothing yields undefined
an awaited async binding gives its value

promise.name: an async binding returns a real promise
promise.script: var p = slow(1, 'a'); var real = p instanceof Promise; await p; return real;

promise.name: the promise has a callable then
promise.script: var p = slow(1, 'a'); var kind = typeof p.then; await p; return kind;

promise.name: a rejected binding is caught by the awaiting script
promise.script: try { await fail('nope'); return 'resolved'; } catch (e) { return e.message.indexOf('nope') !== -1; }

promise.name: the script keeps running while an async binding is pending
promise.script: var order = []; var p = slow(5, 'later').then(function (x) { order.push(x); }); order.push(sync()); await p; return order.join(',');

promise.name: two async bindings are pending at once
promise.script: var p = slow(20, 'a'); var q = slow(1, 'b'); var both = await Promise.all([p, q]); return both.join('');

promise.name: Promise.race settles with the faster binding

syncReach.name: an async binding reached from execute fails naming the binding
syncReach.script: (function () { try { slow(1, 'x'); return 'started'; } catch (e) { return String(e.message); } })()

syncReach.name: an uncaught refusal leaves the runtime usable
syncReach.script: (function () { try { return slow(1, 'x').then(function () { return 'ran'; }); } catch (e) { return String(e.message); } })()
syncReach.after: var a = await slow(1, 'one'); var b = await slow(1, 'two'); return a + b;

executeResult.name: an async function's result is refused
a pending promise result is refused

exportAsync.name: an async export's result is awaited
an export awaiting an async binding gets its value
an export returning a settled promise gives its value
an async binding hands an export a real promise
an export racing async bindings settles with the faster
an export handing back an async binding's promise gives its value

exportSync.name: an export ending in a promise is refused by the synchronous invocation
an async binding an export reaches during a synchronous invocation is refused
